content.value_statement: Developers need clear guidance for Chrome built-in AI before adding local model features. This skill explains Prompt API setup, sessions, streaming, structured output, extensions, and limitations.
actual_capabilities: Explains Chrome and hardware requirements for the built-in Prompt API.
Shows how to check LanguageModel availability and model parameters.
Provides examples for creating sessions with custom parameters and abort signals.
Documents streaming prompts, non-streaming prompts, and response prefixes.
Shows structured output with JSON Schema response constraints.
Summarizes extension support, iframe permissions, local development, and limitations.
limitations: Applies only to Chrome versions and origin trials described in the skill.
Does not install Chrome, enable flags, or download the local model.
Does not provide production security controls for prompt injection or unsafe user input.
Does not cover server-side AI APIs or non-Chrome browsers.

use_cases.title: Prototype Local AI Features
use_cases.description: Build page summarization, classification, and assistant features that run through Chrome built-in AI.

use_cases.title: Plan Chrome Extension AI
use_cases.description: Check extension support, permission cleanup, session patterns, and local model readiness.

use_cases.title: Design Structured Outputs
use_cases.description: Use response constraints to get predictable booleans, lists, and typed summaries from browser prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prompt API Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list the Chrome version, hardware, storage, and availability checks needed before using the Prompt API.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a browser prompt flow with availability checking, LanguageModel.create, a user prompt, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add Streaming and Structured Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Prompt API feature that streams long responses and returns constrained structured data.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit my Prompt API design for quota handling, session cleanup, localStorage use, iframe policy, and unsupported environments.

output_examples.input: I need a readiness checklist for a Prompt API demo.
output: Confirm Chrome 138 or later on desktop.
Verify storage, memory, GPU, and unmetered download access.
Check availability before creating a session.
Prepare fallback states for unavailable or downloading models.

output_examples.input: I am adding AI to a Chrome extension.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends checking stable extension support, removing expired origin trial permissions, managing sessions carefully, and adding clear unavailable states.

output_examples.input: I need structured hashtag output for posts.
output_examples.output: The skill guides you to define a response constraint, request a short result, parse the response, and validate the result.

best_practices: Check availability with the same options used for session creation.
Use streaming, abort signals, and quota checks for long user-facing responses.
Destroy unused sessions and keep fallback states for unsupported devices.
anti_patterns: Creating sessions before checking availability or user activation.
Saving long conversations without managing quota and privacy impact.
Assuming desktop Chrome support also means mobile or worker support.

faq.question: Does this skill call external AI services?
faq.answer: No. It documents Chrome built-in Prompt API behavior for local Gemini Nano use in the browser.

faq.question: Can it make my app work on mobile Chrome?
faq.answer: No. The source states mobile platforms are not supported.

faq.question: Does it include Chrome Extension guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers extension support, obsolete origin trial permissions, and permission policy basics.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns, but you should review security, privacy, and browser compatibility before release.

faq.question: Does it cover multimodal input?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes text, image, and audio inputs where origin trial support is available.

faq.question: What should I check first?
faq.answer: Check Chrome version, hardware, storage, network access, and LanguageModel availability before creating a session.
